newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Winbond gets T$3.03 bln for fire loss.
newsitem.headline: Winbond gets T$3.03 bln for fire loss.

text.p: Winbond Electronics Corp, one of Taiwan's leading semiconductor makers, said on Wednesday it had gained a T$3.03 billion in fire insurance compensation for a fire loss occured in October 1996.

"Nine co-insurance firms have agreed to pay Winbond for a fire insurance compensation worth T$3.03 billion, a fund that will help us rebuild our plant," Hander Chang, Winbond spokesman and assistant vice-president, told Reuters.

He said Winbond had total claims of T$7.4 billion for the fire loss, including T$3.7 billion in fire insurance, and another T$3.7 billion in erection-all-risk insurance, or insurance that covers equipment installation.

The nine co-insurance firms eventually agreed to pay T$3.03 billion out of the claimed T$3.7 billion for fire insurance, but five co-insurers which cover erection-all-risk insurance still declined to pay, Chang said.
The nine co-insurance firms include Tai Ping Insurance, Fubon Insurance, Central Insurance, Mingtai Fire and Marine Insurance and Shin Kong Insurance, he said.
In early May, Winbond said it filed civil litigation against five insurance firms, requesting T$1.4 billion for a fire loss that occurred in October 1996.
Winbond said in a statement that the request for T$1.4 billion was the first round out of the total loss claims of T$3.7 billion that should be covered in its erection-all-risk insurance.
"It's strange that the five insurance firms are among the nine insurers that cover fire insurance, but the latter agree to pay while the former decline," Chang said.
Winbond said it filed the suit after seven months of unsatisfactory negotiation with insurers regarding the insurance claims on the fire at an unfinished wafer fabrication plant.
Chang said Winbond expect to complete construction of the plant in early 1999, delayed from early 1997 due to the fire.
